subject: Critical Thinking
title: Red Herring: Changing the Subject
description: A quick win: understand Red Herring: Changing the Subject.

hook.text: 'Why did you miss the deadline?' 'Well, the whole project was poorly planned from the start.' The subject just changed.

buildup.text: Red herring: introducing an irrelevant topic to divert attention from the original issue.

discovery.text: The name comes from smoked herring, which was dragged across trails to mislead hunting dogs.

twist.text: Red herrings are powerful because the diversion is often interesting.

climax.text: Politicians are masters: 'What about your tax plan?' 'Let me tell you about my opponent's record on...' Redirect.

punchline.text: An interesting answer to the wrong question is still no answer.

quiz.question: What makes a red herring effective?
options: The diversion is interesting enough that people forget the original question

details.summary: A red herring introduces an irrelevant topic to divert attention from the original argument. The distraction succeeds when the new topic is interesting enough that the audience forgets the original point was never addressed.
details.whyItMatters: Politicians and debaters use red herrings constantly to avoid difficult questions. Recognizing the tactic keeps discussions on track and accountability intact.
takeaways: Red herrings divert attention from the real issue
The diversion is often more interesting than the original topic
Returning to the original question is the simple counter

faq.question: How do you counter a red herring during a discussion?
faq.answer: Acknowledge the new point briefly but redirect: 'That is interesting, but it does not address the original question, which was...' Keeping a visible record of the original question helps prevent successful diversions.

faq.question: Why is the red herring named after a type of fish?
faq.answer: The name comes from the practice of using strongly scented smoked fish to train hunting dogs. A red herring dragged across the trail would distract dogs from the original scent, just as the fallacy distracts from the original argument.
